title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer at Scale
hook: What if a robot's controller was trained like a language model — on huge, diverse, task-agnostic data? Performance starts scaling with model size and data.
key_points: A transformer-based model for real-world robotic control.
Trained on large, diverse, task-agnostic robot demonstration datasets.
Argues open-ended, task-agnostic training plus high-capacity architectures enables generalization in robotics.
Shows performance scales with model size and data diversity on real robots doing real tasks.
content_html: Anthony Brohan, Noah Brown, Justice Carbajal, and colleagues introduce RT-1, a transformer-based model for controlling real robots in the physical world. They train it on large, diverse, task-agnostic datasets of robot demonstrations, arguing that this open-ended style of training — paired with a high-capacity architecture — is what lets robots generalize rather than memorize a few hard-coded skills.
extra_html:
How it works

RT-1 brings the recipe behind large language and vision models to robotics: collect a lot of varied data, then train a high-capacity transformer on it. The demonstrations are task-agnostic, gathered at scale from real robots performing real-world tasks rather than narrow scripted routines. Because the architecture has the capacity to absorb that diversity, the model learns broadly useful control rather than overfitting to a single setup.

Why it matters

The headline finding is that robotics behaves like other deep-learning domains: performance scales with model size and data diversity. That reframes the path forward — instead of engineering one behavior at a time, you can push capability by collecting more diverse data and training bigger models. It sets up the vision-language-action approach that RT-2 later builds on.

related.title: RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models
related.hook: Treat a robot's actions as just more text tokens, and a vision-language model can learn to act — carrying its web knowledge into the physical world.

related.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words (ViT)
related.hook: Chop an image into patches, treat each like a word, and feed them to a plain Transformer. With enough pretraining data, it matches or beats convolutional networks.
